Maturation: 1 month | Yield = about 1 pint of pickle | Image = [[Image:Lemon pickle star anise.jpg|300px]] }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Cuisine of India]] '''Lemon pickle''' is a traditional condiment used with [[Cookbook:Cuisine of India|Indian]] food. Many pickle recipes from India have oil to help preserve the pickle, but this recipe uses no oil. {{see also|Cookbook:Lemon Pickle I}} ==Ingredients== * 8 small or 4 large [[Cookbook:Lemon|lemons]] * ½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] * ¼–½ cup [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] * 4 small green [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], finely [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tablespoon]] [[Cookbook:Mustard|yellow mustard]] seed * 1 tablespoon ground [[Cookbook:Ginger|ginger]] * 1 [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|teaspoon]] [[Cookbook:Fenugreek|fenugreek]] seed * ¼ teaspoon [[Cookbook:Turmeric|turmeric]] powder * 1–2 [[Cookbook:Star Anise|star anise]] pods ==Procedure== # Cut lemons into small pieces, and place in a bowl. # Cover with salt and set aside for at least 4 hours (24 is better). # Dry-roast the yellow mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, star anise, and chopped chilis in a pan over high heat, shaking constantly—don't burn them! # Strain the juice from the lemons into a small [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]], add the turmeric, ginger and sugar, and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] for 2–3 minutes until the sugar has dissolved. If there isn't enough juice, add 1–2 tablespoons water. # Add the spices and sugar mixture to the bowl of lemons, and mix together well. # Pack into a pint jar, pressing the pieces in if needed, to ensure that the liquid covers all the lemon pieces. # Set aside to mature for 1 month. ==Notes, tips and variations== * If you don't have fresh chilis, add some dried chilis or chili powder. The pickle in the photo has three whole dried chilis in it. steps.text: Cut lemons into small pieces, and place in a bowl.
Cover with salt and set aside for at least 4 hours (24 is better).
Dry-roast the yellow mustard seeds, fenugreek seeds, star anise, and chopped chilis in a pan over high heat, shaking constantly—don't burn them!

Strain the juice from the lemons into a small saucepan, add the turmeric, ginger and sugar, and simmer for 2–3 minutes until the sugar has dissolved. If there isn't enough juice, add 1–2 tablespoons water.
Add the spices and sugar mixture to the bowl of lemons, and mix together well.
Pack into a pint jar, pressing the pieces in if needed, to ensure that the liquid covers all the lemon pieces.
Set aside to mature for 1 month.
